key_insight: A native 2D pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz can be more expressive and initially more trainable than comparable 1D entanglement patterns on 16 qubits.
engineering_relevance: For hardware with planar connectivity, matching the ansatz to the device topology can improve early optimization behavior without increasing conceptual complexity.
method: Built a 2D pairwise PQC aligned with planar superconducting-qubit layouts.
Compared it against three representative 1D ansatze at the same layer depths on 16 qubits.
Evaluated expressibility via KL divergence and second-order frame potential, and trainability via gradient-variance measurements.
evidence_signal: At shallow depths, the 2D ansatz showed the lowest KL divergence at L=1 and L=2, reached the frame-potential lower bound faster, and had smaller Pauli-Z-string gradient variance for L=1–4.
watch_item: The advantage narrows as depth increases, so the benefit may be most relevant at shallow circuits and could depend on the chosen observable and parameterization.
paper_title: Expressibility and trainability of a two-dimensional pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz
